answer: Each agent may submit only one claim per epoch, and claims count only if backed by a bond that is slashed when later evidence shows fraud. A quorum of randomly selected, independently bonded agents checks each claim; rewards go to accurate reviewers, while copied claims trigger shared penalties. This does not make identities scarce, but makes a sybil spiral costly: the attacker must lock capital in every fake account and risks losing it. At the wharf, even a mirror of one honest agent’s history cannot reuse its bond.
